label: Ethical Wildlife Encounters in the Philippines
title: Ethical Wildlife Encounters in the Philippines
description: Whale sharks without the feeding, tarsiers without the flash, dolphins and turtles without the chase: where to go and the rules that protect them.
intro: Swimming next to a whale shark is one of the best things you can do in the Philippines. How you do it matters. Here's where the animals show up on their own terms, and the rules that keep it that way.

faqs.question: Is Oslob whale shark watching ethical?
faqs.answer: Oslob works because the sharks are hand-fed krill every morning. Peer-reviewed studies found the feeding changes how the sharks dive and how long they stay, and scars were seen on 95% of sharks identified there. Donsol and Pintuyan rely on sharks that come naturally in season.

faqs.question: When can I see whale sharks in Donsol and Pintuyan?
faqs.answer: LAMAVE puts the Donsol season at November to May and the Southern Leyte (Pintuyan) season at November to June. Sightings are never guaranteed, because the sharks are wild.

faqs.question: How close can I get to a whale shark?
faqs.answer: In Donsol, keep at least 3 m from the head and 4 m from the tail. No touching, riding, feeding or flash photos anywhere.

faqs.question: Where should I see tarsiers in Bohol?
faqs.answer: Go to the Philippine Tarsier Sanctuary in Corella. Some tours stop at less ethical tarsier exhibits in Loboc instead, so check your itinerary and never use flash.

sections.heading: The short version
sections.body:
- **Whale sharks:** go to [Donsol](/places/donsol/donsol-whale-shark-interaction) or [Pintuyan](/places/pintuyan/pintuyan-whale-shark-interaction) in season, not a feeding site.
- **Tarsiers:** only the [Philippine Tarsier Sanctuary in Corella](/places/corella/philippine-tarsier-sanctuary-corella). No flash, no touching.
- **Dolphins:** boats keep their distance and never chase. You stay on board.
- **Sea turtles:** look, don't touch. At [Apo Island](/places/dauin/apo-island-dauin) you're inside a protected seascape.
- **Anywhere:** if a tour promises a guaranteed sighting or a selfie with a wild animal, that's your cue to walk away.

sections.heading: Whale sharks: why we don't list Oslob
sections.body:
Oslob in Cebu runs what LAMAVE, the Philippine marine research group, calls the largest non-captive provisioned whale shark interaction in the world. Translation: fishermen hand-feed krill to the sharks every morning, roughly 6 AM to 1 PM, and more than 500,000 tourists come to watch each year.

The science on it is not pretty:

- On feeding days the sharks spent about six times more of the morning at the surface, and researchers warn this could affect the health of sharks that visit often (Scientific Reports, 2020).
- Some sharks stopped migrating and became year-round residents, a clear response to the feeding (Royal Society Open Science, 2017).
- In 93% of in-water surveys, people were closer than 2 m to a shark, even though the local rules ban touching (Royal Society Open Science, 2020).
- Scars were seen on 95% of the whale sharks identified at Oslob, compared with 27% in Australia (LAMAVE, 2019).

That's why Oslob is not on GalaTayo. You can have the same jaw-drop moment somewhere the sharks turn up by choice.

sections.heading: Whale sharks done right: Donsol and Pintuyan
sections.body:
**[Donsol, Sorsogon](/places/donsol/donsol-whale-shark-interaction)** was the country's first whale shark tourism site, started in 1998. The sharks gather in the bay to feed from November to May, and trained Butanding Interaction Officers guide every boat. The rules are simple: keep at least 3 m from the head and 4 m from the tail, and never touch, ride or feed a shark. Fair warning: wild means no guarantees. WWF-Philippines records showed a 68% drop in sightings from 2017 to 2018, so give yourself more than one morning.

**[Pintuyan, Southern Leyte](/places/pintuyan/pintuyan-whale-shark-interaction)** is run by a local community group, KASAKA, and LAMAVE's research calls Southern Leyte the most sustainable whale shark tourism model in the Philippines. Keep 3 m away, skip the flash and selfie sticks, and only get in the water when the spotter says jump. The town charges ₱300 per visitor, and interactions pause from June 1 until they reopen in October.

sections.heading: Thresher sharks in Malapascua
sections.body: [Malapascua](/places/daanbantayan/malapascua-thresher-shark-dive) is famous for pelagic thresher sharks that come up from deep water to get cleaned by small fish on a seamount. Researchers found that arriving divers interrupted some of these cleaning visits (PLoS ONE, 2011), so dive with an operator that keeps groups calm and still. Most thresher dives now head to Kimud Shoal, about an hour by boat, after sightings at Monad Shoal dropped around 2022.

sections.heading: Tarsiers: tiny, nocturnal and easily stressed
sections.body: The Philippine tarsier is a small nocturnal primate found only in the Philippines. See them at the [Philippine Tarsier Sanctuary in Corella](/places/corella/philippine-tarsier-sanctuary-corella), about 30 to 45 minutes from Tagbilaran. Some Bohol countryside tours stop at less ethical tarsier exhibits in Loboc instead, so ask before you book and make sure yours goes to Corella. Inside, keep your voice down and your flash off.

sections.heading: Dolphins: let them come to you
sections.body:
Philippine rules for watching dolphins and whales (BFAR-NFRDI, DA and DOT, 2004) are clear, and good operators follow them:

- Boats never approach head-on under power or drive into a group.
- A powered boat may follow dolphins or whales for no more than 20 minutes.
- Boats stay at least 100 m from any whale.
- Operators must not let passengers swim with them.

Island-hopping trips around [Balicasag](/places/panglao/balicasag-island-panglao) off Panglao often add dolphin watching. If your boatman starts chasing a pod, it's fine to ask him to back off.

sections.heading: Sea turtles: look, don't touch
sections.body:
[Apo Island](/places/dauin/apo-island-dauin) is a protected landscape and seascape under Philippine law, with a community-run marine sanctuary that Greenpeace calls one of the best of its kind. Sea turtles feed around the island. Don't touch, chase or flash-photograph them, and keep your distance. The Wildlife Act (Republic Act 9147) also makes collecting, hunting, possessing or trading wildlife illegal, so leave every shell and souvenir made from turtles on the shelf.

The national rules for marine wildlife tourism (Joint Memorandum Circular No. 1, 2020) ban any act that disturbs, harasses or mistreats marine wildlife. That covers whale sharks, dolphins and turtles alike.

label: Is the Philippines Safe? Where to Go and What to Know (2026)
title: Is the Philippines Safe? Where to Go (2026)
keywords: is the philippines safe for tourists
description: What the UK and Canadian travel advisories actually say, which regions they flag, the scams to know, typhoon season and the places we list.
intro: Short answer: most of the places travellers actually go are covered by normal-caution advice. The official warnings focus on specific parts of Mindanao and the Sulu archipelago. Here's what they say, word for word where it matters.

faqs.question: Is the Philippines safe for tourists in 2026?
faqs.answer: Canada rates the Philippines 'exercise a high degree of caution' with regional advisories, and the UK's warnings centre on Mindanao and the Sulu archipelago. Luzon and the Visayas, where most tourist spots are, are not under those regional warnings.

faqs.question: Which parts of the Philippines should I avoid?
faqs.answer: The UK advises against all travel to western and central Mindanao and the Sulu archipelago, and against all but essential travel to the rest of Mindanao, except Camiguin, Dinagat and Siargao. Canada names specific Mindanao provinces and excludes Davao City and Siargao Island.

faqs.question: Is Siargao safe to visit?
faqs.answer: Both the UK and Canada carve Siargao out of their Mindanao warnings. Normal precautions apply: Cloud 9 is a shallow reef break with no lifeguards.

faqs.question: What is the emergency number in the Philippines?
faqs.answer: Dial 911, the national emergency hotline since 2016.

faqs.question: When is typhoon season in the Philippines?
faqs.answer: PAGASA counts about 20 tropical cyclones a year in the Philippine Area of Responsibility, with the peak from July to October.

sections.heading: What the official advisories say
sections.body:
We checked the government pages themselves on 12 October 2026.

- **United Kingdom (FCDO), updated 15 July 2026:** advises against all travel to western and central Mindanao and the Sulu archipelago, and against all but essential travel to the rest of Mindanao, except Camiguin, Dinagat and Siargao islands.
- **Canada, updated 7 July 2026:** exercise a high degree of caution, with regional advisories. Avoid all travel to western Mindanao provinces including Basilan, Sulu, Tawi-Tawi, Maguindanao and the Zamboanga provinces. Avoid non-essential travel to central and eastern Mindanao, excluding Davao City and Siargao Island.
- **United States and Australia:** both publish their own level-based advice at travel.state.gov and smartraveller.gov.au. Their pages didn't load for us, so we're not quoting them. Check them before you fly.

The pattern is the same everywhere: the warnings are about specific regions, not the whole country.

sections.heading: Where we send travellers
sections.body:
These picks all sit outside those regional warnings:

- **Manila:** [Intramuros](/places/manila/intramuros) and [Fort Santiago](/places/manila/fort-santiago) for a heritage day.
- **Palawan:** [El Nido's lagoons](/places/el-nido/el-nido-tour-a-lagoons) and [Kayangan Lake in Coron](/places/coron/kayangan-lake-coron).
- **Visayas:** [White Beach Boracay](/places/malay-boracay/white-beach-boracay), the [Chocolate Hills](/places/carmen-bohol/chocolate-hills-carmen) and [Alona Beach](/places/panglao/alona-beach-panglao) in Bohol.
- **North Luzon:** [Calle Crisologo in Vigan](/places/vigan/calle-crisologo-vigan), the [Batad rice terraces](/places/banaue/batad-rice-terraces-banaue) and the [Hundred Islands](/places/alaminos/hundred-islands-national-park-alaminos).
- **Mindanao's island exceptions:** [Cloud 9 in Siargao](/places/general-luna-siargao/cloud-9-siargao) and [White Island in Camiguin](/places/camiguin/white-island-camiguin), both carved out of the UK warning.

Each place page has a Know before you go block with fees, how to get there and the rough-weather months.

sections.heading: Scams and petty crime to know
sections.body:
None of this is unique to the Philippines, but these are the ones the advisories call out:

- **Taxis:** use taxis from a reputable company, including to and from the airport, and insist on the meter. Canada suggests hotel transport, official airport taxis or a ride-hailing app. Grab works in Manila, Cebu, Davao, Iloilo, Baguio, Dumaguete and more.
- **Too-friendly strangers:** be careful when strangers offer friendship. Canada reports solo tourists being drugged and robbed after an invitation to visit an attraction.
- **Cards and ATMs:** credit card and ATM fraud happens often. Keep an eye on your card when you pay.
- **Pickpockets:** pickpocketing, swarming and bag snatching happen, mostly in cities. Don't flash cash or jewellery on public transport.
- **Drinks:** methanol in alcoholic drinks can kill even in small amounts, and you can't taste or smell it.
- **Tourist-trap pricing:** in Intramuros the official kalesa rate is ₱1,000 per trip (2024), and in Boracay sharing an e-trike avoids overcharging. Agree the price before you ride.

sections.heading: Typhoons, quakes and volcanoes
sections.body:
Nature is the bigger planning factor. PAGASA counts about 20 tropical cyclones a year in the Philippine Area of Responsibility, with the peak from July to October. The UK notes that ferry accidents are more frequent in the June to December rainy season, when storms can develop quickly, so leave a spare day around island hops.

Earthquakes happen regularly; a magnitude 6.9 quake hit northern Cebu near Bogo City on 30 September 2025. Any volcano can erupt without warning, and entry to Mayon's 6-km Permanent Danger Zone is banned even at Alert Level 1. Check PAGASA for weather and PHIVOLCS for quakes and volcanoes before a big trip.

sections.heading: On the water
sections.body: Island hopping is the highlight of most trips, so take the boring bits seriously. Beaches often have no lifeguards or warning signs, and the UK notes the ferry network has a poor maritime safety record. Wear the life vest (it is mandatory on El Nido tour boats), accept it when a gale warning cancels your trip, and swim with a buddy or guide at shore-entry snorkel spots.

sections.heading: Before you land
sections.body:
- **eTravel:** all travellers must register their entry and exit on the official eTravel system (etravel.gov.ph) within 72 hours before travel. Registration is free, so ignore sites that charge for it.
- **Emergencies:** dial 911.
- **Drugs:** penalties for importing and using illegal drugs are very severe.
